Compliance · EU

In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation

Regulation (EU) 2017/746 · applies since 2022-05-26 (transitional dates up to 2030) · mandatory-for-scope · official text (free)

Applies to: Manufacturers of in vitro diagnostic devices and their software placed on the EU market.

A check shows a breach in code; it does not certify that a point is met. List scraped from the publisher's document on 2026-11-01. A point here means: Article, numbered paragraph and lettered or roman point at every depth; Annex, its Parts, Sections and Chapters, and its numbered points. Recitals, footnotes, amendment markers and correlation tables left out (consolidated text 02017R0746-20250110).

Art. 1 Subject matter and scope
Art. 1(1) Sets the regulation's scope: placing, making available and putting into service of IVD devices, plus performance studies. Coming soon
Art. 1(2) Defines 'devices' as shorthand for IVD medical devices and their accessories. Coming soon
Art. 1(3) Introduces the list of products excluded from the regulation.
Art. 1(3)(a) Excludes general laboratory and research-only products unless the manufacturer intends diagnostic use. Coming soon
Art. 1(3)(b) Excludes invasive sampling products and products applied to the body to obtain specimens. Coming soon
Art. 1(3)(c) Excludes internationally certified reference materials. Coming soon
Art. 1(3)(d) Excludes materials used in external quality assessment schemes. Coming soon
Art. 1(4) Devices embedding a medical device fall under the medical device regulation; this one covers the IVD part. Coming soon
Art. 1(5) States this regulation is specific Union legislation under the EMC directive. Coming soon
Art. 1(6) Devices that are also machinery must meet more specific machinery safety requirements where a hazard exists. Coming soon
Art. 1(7) Confirms the regulation does not affect the Euratom radiation protection directive. Coming soon
Art. 1(8) Preserves Member States' right to restrict use of device types on matters outside this regulation. Coming soon
Art. 1(9) Preserves national law on organisation, delivery and financing of healthcare, including prescription requirements. Coming soon
Art. 1(10) Protects press freedom and freedom of expression in the media. Coming soon
Art. 2 DefinitionsIntroduces the definitions used in the regulation.
Art. 2(1) Defines medical device by reference to the medical devices regulation. Coming soon
Art. 2(2) Defines an in vitro diagnostic device, including software, examining human specimens for medical information.
Art. 2(2)(a) Information on a physiological or pathological process or state. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(b) Information on congenital physical or mental impairments. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(c) Information on predisposition to a condition or disease. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(d) Determining safety and compatibility with potential recipients. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(e) Predicting treatment response or reactions. Coming soon
Art. 2(2)(f) Defining or monitoring therapeutic measures. Coming soon
Art. 2(3) Defines specimen receptacle as a container for holding and preserving specimens for diagnostic examination. Coming soon
Art. 2(4) Defines accessory as an article enabling or directly assisting an IVD device's intended use. Coming soon
Art. 2(5) Defines self-testing device as one intended for lay persons. Coming soon
Art. 2(6) Defines near-patient testing device used by professionals outside a laboratory. Coming soon
Art. 2(7) Defines companion diagnostic as essential for safe and effective use of a medicinal product.
Art. 2(7)(a) Identifying patients most likely to benefit from the medicinal product. Coming soon
Art. 2(7)(b) Identifying patients at increased risk of serious adverse reactions. Coming soon
Art. 2(8) Defines generic device group by shared purpose or technology. Coming soon
Art. 2(9) Defines single-use device as intended for one procedure. Coming soon
Art. 2(10) Defines falsified device as one with false identity, source or certification presentation. Coming soon
Art. 2(11) Defines kit as packaged components for a specific diagnostic examination. Coming soon
Art. 2(12) Defines intended purpose from manufacturer's label, instructions, promotion or performance evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 2(13) Defines label as written, printed or graphic information on device or packaging. Coming soon
Art. 2(14) Defines instructions for use as manufacturer information on purpose, proper use and precautions. Coming soon
Art. 2(15) Defines Unique Device Identifier as a standardised code identifying specific devices. Coming soon
Art. 2(16) Defines risk as probability of harm combined with its severity. Coming soon
Art. 2(17) Defines benefit-risk determination as analysis of benefits and risks for intended use. Coming soon
Art. 2(18) Defines compatibility of a device or software used with other devices.
Art. 2(18)(a) Performing as intended without loss of ability. Coming soon
Art. 2(18)(b) Integrating or operating without modifying combined devices. Coming soon
Art. 2(18)(c) Being used together without conflict, interference or adverse reaction. Coming soon
Art. 2(19) Defines interoperability between devices or software.
Art. 2(19)(a) Exchanging and using information without altering data content. Coming soon
Art. 2(19)(b) Communicating with each other. Coming soon
Art. 2(19)(c) Working together as intended. Coming soon
Art. 2(20) Defines making available on the market as commercial supply in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 2(21) Defines placing on the market as first making available in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 2(22) Defines putting into service as first readiness for final user's intended use. Coming soon
Art. 2(23) Defines manufacturer as who makes or has made a device and markets it under own name. Coming soon
Art. 2(24) Defines full refurbishing as complete rebuilding with a new lifetime. Coming soon
Art. 2(25) Defines authorised representative as Union-based party mandated by a non-Union manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 2(26) Defines importer as Union-based party placing third-country devices on the market. Coming soon
Art. 2(27) Defines distributor as a supply-chain party other than manufacturer or importer. Coming soon
Art. 2(28) Defines economic operator as manufacturer, representative, importer or distributor. Coming soon
Art. 2(29) Defines health institution as an organisation for patient care or public health. Coming soon
Art. 2(30) Defines user as any healthcare professional or lay person using a device. Coming soon
Art. 2(31) Defines lay person as someone without formal healthcare education. Coming soon
Art. 2(32) Defines conformity assessment as the process showing requirements are met. Coming soon
Art. 2(33) Defines conformity assessment body as a third-party testing, certification and inspection body. Coming soon
Art. 2(34) Defines notified body as a designated conformity assessment body. Coming soon
Art. 2(35) Defines CE marking as the manufacturer's indication of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 2(36) Defines clinical evidence as clinical data and performance results sufficient to assess safety and benefit. Coming soon
Art. 2(37) Defines clinical benefit as positive impact on patient management, diagnosis or public health. Coming soon
Art. 2(38) Defines scientific validity of an analyte as its association with a condition. Coming soon
Art. 2(39) Defines device performance as ability to achieve its claimed purpose. Coming soon
Art. 2(40) Defines analytical performance as correctly detecting or measuring an analyte. Coming soon
Art. 2(41) Defines clinical performance as yielding results correlated with a clinical condition. Coming soon
Art. 2(42) Defines performance study as a study establishing analytical or clinical performance. Coming soon
Art. 2(43) Defines performance study plan as the document describing a study's design and conduct. Coming soon
Art. 2(44) Defines performance evaluation as assessment of scientific validity and performance data. Coming soon
Art. 2(45) Defines device for performance study; research without medical objective is excluded. Coming soon
Art. 2(46) Defines interventional clinical performance study as one whose results may influence patient management. Coming soon
Art. 2(47) Defines subject as a performance study participant whose specimens are examined. Coming soon
Art. 2(48) Defines investigator as the person responsible for a study at a site. Coming soon
Art. 2(49) Defines diagnostic specificity as recognising absence of a target marker. Coming soon
Art. 2(50) Defines diagnostic sensitivity as identifying presence of a target marker. Coming soon
Art. 2(51) Defines predictive value as probability that a test result reflects the condition. Coming soon
Art. 2(52) Defines positive predictive value as separating true from false positives. Coming soon
Art. 2(53) Defines negative predictive value as separating true from false negatives. Coming soon
Art. 2(54) Defines likelihood ratio comparing result likelihood with and without the condition. Coming soon
Art. 2(55) Defines calibrator as a measurement reference material for calibration. Coming soon
Art. 2(56) Defines control material as used to verify a device's performance characteristics. Coming soon
Art. 2(57) Defines sponsor as the party responsible for initiating, managing and funding a performance study. Coming soon
Art. 2(58) Defines informed consent as free, informed willingness to join a performance study. Coming soon
Art. 2(59) Defines ethics committee as an independent body giving opinions under the regulation. Coming soon
Art. 2(60) Defines adverse event in a performance study context. Coming soon
Art. 2(61) Defines serious adverse event by listed severe outcomes.
Art. 2(61)(a) Patient management decision causing death or imminent life-threatening situation. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(b) Death. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(c) Serious deterioration of health leading to listed consequences.
Art. 2(61)(c)(i) Life-threatening illness or injury. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(c)(ii) Permanent impairment of a body structure or function. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(c)(iii) Hospitalisation or longer hospital stay. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(c)(iv) Intervention to prevent life-threatening illness or permanent impairment. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(c)(v) Chronic disease. Coming soon
Art. 2(61)(d) Foetal distress or death, congenital impairment or birth defect. Coming soon
Art. 2(62) Defines device deficiency as inadequacy in a study device's quality, safety or information. Coming soon
Art. 2(63) Defines post-market surveillance as systematic proactive collection of experience from marketed devices. Coming soon
Art. 2(64) Defines market surveillance as public authority checks that devices comply. Coming soon
Art. 2(65) Defines recall as returning a device already with the end user. Coming soon
Art. 2(66) Defines withdrawal as stopping a device in the supply chain from being supplied. Coming soon
Art. 2(67) Defines incident as malfunction, deterioration, information inadequacy or harm from device-based decisions. Coming soon
Art. 2(68) Defines serious incident by potential outcomes listed below.
Art. 2(68)(a) Death of a patient, user or other person. Coming soon
Art. 2(68)(b) Serious temporary or permanent deterioration of health. Coming soon
Art. 2(68)(c) A serious public health threat. Coming soon
Art. 2(69) Defines serious public health threat as an event risking death, serious illness or unusual morbidity. Coming soon
Art. 2(70) Defines corrective action as eliminating the cause of non-conformity. Coming soon
Art. 2(71) Defines field safety corrective action by manufacturer to reduce serious incident risk. Coming soon
Art. 2(72) Defines field safety notice as manufacturer communication about a corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 2(73) Defines harmonised standard by reference to the standardisation regulation. Coming soon
Art. 2(74) Defines common specifications as technical or clinical requirements other than a standard. Coming soon
Art. 3 Regulatory status of products
Art. 3(1) Commission decides by implementing act, on Member State request, whether a product is an IVD or accessory. Coming soon
Art. 3(2) Commission may decide product regulatory status on its own initiative after consulting MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 3(3) Commission ensures Member States share expertise across product fields to determine regulatory status. Coming soon
Art. 3(4) Commission consults EMA, ECHA and EFSA when status involves medicines, tissues, biocides or food. Coming soon
Art. 4 Genetic information, counselling and informed consent
Art. 4(1) Member States must ensure people receiving genetic tests get information on the test's nature and implications. Coming soon
Art. 4(2) Member States must ensure counselling is available for genetic tests revealing predisposition to untreatable conditions. Coming soon
Art. 4(3) Counselling duty does not apply to confirming a known diagnosis or to companion diagnostics. Coming soon
Art. 4(4) Member States may keep or adopt more protective national rules, including on informed consent. Coming soon
Art. 5 Placing on the market and putting into service
Art. 5(1) Devices may be marketed or put into service only if compliant when properly supplied and used. Coming soon
Art. 5(2) Devices must satisfy applicable Annex I safety and performance requirements for their intended purpose. Coming soon
Art. 5(3) Proving conformity with safety and performance requirements must include a performance evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 5(4) Devices made and used inside health institutions count as put into service. Coming soon
Art. 5(5) In-house devices in health institutions are exempt from most rules if listed conditions are met.
Art. 5(5)(a) In-house devices must not be transferred to another legal entity. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(b) In-house devices must be made and used under suitable quality management systems. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(c) The institution's laboratory must comply with the medical laboratory standard or national equivalent provisions. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(d) Institution must document why patient needs cannot be met by an equivalent marketed device. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(e) Institution must give its authority, on request, information and justification about in-house device use. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(f) Institution must publish a declaration about its in-house devices.
Art. 5(5)(f)(i) Public declaration must give the manufacturing institution's name and address. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(f)(ii) Public declaration must include details identifying the devices. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(f)(iii) Declaration must state Annex I requirements are met, with justified exceptions. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(g) For class D in-house devices, institution must keep documentation on facility, process, design and performance. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(h) Institution must ensure devices are made according to the required documentation. Coming soon
Art. 5(5)(i) Institution must review clinical use experience and take corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 5(6) Commission may adopt implementing acts to resolve divergent interpretation of Annex I. Coming soon
Art. 6 Distance sales
Art. 6(1) Devices offered online to persons in the Union must comply with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 6(2) Devices used for remote diagnostic services to Union persons must comply with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 6(3) On authority request, remote sellers or service providers must supply the declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 6(4) Member States may require an online service provider to stop for public health. Coming soon
Art. 7 ClaimsLabelling, instructions and advertising must not mislead about the device's purpose, safety or performance.
Art. 7(a) Must not attribute functions or properties the device lacks. Coming soon
Art. 7(b) Must not create a false impression about diagnosis, treatment or capabilities. Coming soon
Art. 7(c) Must not omit likely risks of using the device as intended. Coming soon
Art. 7(d) Must not suggest uses outside the assessed intended purpose. Coming soon
Art. 8 Use of harmonised standards
Art. 8(1) Conformity with published harmonised standards gives presumption of conformity with covered requirements. Coming soon
Art. 8(2) European Pharmacopoeia monographs published in the Official Journal count as harmonised standards. Coming soon
Art. 9 Common specifications
Art. 9(1) Commission may adopt common specifications where standards are missing or insufficient. Coming soon
Art. 9(2) Devices meeting common specifications are presumed conformant for the matters covered. Coming soon
Art. 9(3) Manufacturers must follow common specifications unless they justify an equivalent solution. Coming soon
Art. 10 General obligations of manufacturers
Art. 10(1) Manufacturers must design and make devices in line with the Regulation. Coming soon
Art. 10(2) Manufacturers must establish, document and maintain a risk management system. Coming soon
Art. 10(3) Manufacturers must perform performance evaluation, including post-market performance follow-up. Coming soon
Art. 10(4) Manufacturers must draw up and keep current technical documentation. Coming soon
Art. 10(5) After demonstrating compliance, manufacturers issue a declaration of conformity and affix CE marking. Coming soon
Art. 10(6) Manufacturers must meet unique device identification and registration obligations. Coming soon
Art. 10(7) Manufacturers must retain technical documentation and declarations for at least ten years. Coming soon
Art. 10(8) Manufacturers must run a quality management system covering specified aspects, proportionate to risk.
Art. 10(8)(a) Quality system must include a regulatory compliance strategy and change management. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(b) Quality system must identify applicable safety and performance requirements and options to meet them. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(c) Quality system must define management responsibility. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(d) Quality system must cover resource management, including supplier and subcontractor control. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(e) Quality system must include risk management. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(f) Quality system must cover performance evaluation and follow-up. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(g) Quality system must cover product realisation from planning through service provision. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(h) Quality system must verify UDI assignment and consistency of registered information. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(i) Quality system must include a post-market surveillance system. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(j) Quality system must handle communication with authorities, bodies and stakeholders. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(k) Quality system must include processes for reporting serious incidents and field corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(l) Quality system must manage corrective and preventive actions and check their effectiveness. Coming soon
Art. 10(8)(m) Quality system must monitor output, analyse data and drive product improvement. Coming soon
Art. 10(9) Manufacturers must implement and maintain a post-market surveillance system. Coming soon
Art. 10(10) Devices must carry required information in the required languages, with legible, understandable labels. Coming soon
Art. 10(11) Manufacturers must promptly correct, withdraw or recall nonconforming devices and notify relevant parties. Coming soon
Art. 10(12) Manufacturers must have a system for recording and reporting incidents and field corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 10(13) Manufacturers must give authorities requested conformity information, samples and cooperation. Coming soon
Art. 10(14) Identity of any third party designing or making devices must be submitted at registration. Coming soon
Art. 10(15) Manufacturers must have proportionate financial coverage for liability for defective devices. Coming soon
Art. 10a Obligations in case of interruption or discontinuation of supply of certain devices
Art. 10a(1) Manufacturers must give six months' notice of supply interruption that risks serious harm. Coming soon
Art. 10a(2) Receiving authority must inform other Member States and the Commission of anticipated interruption. Coming soon
Art. 10a(3) Economic operators informed of an interruption must pass it on to their direct customers. Coming soon
Art. 11 Authorised representative
Art. 11(1) Non-EU manufacturers must designate a single authorised representative before marketing in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 11(2) Designation is the mandate, valid when accepted in writing, covering a generic device group. Coming soon
Art. 11(3) The mandate must enable the representative to perform specified tasks.
Art. 11(3)(a) Representative verifies the declaration of conformity, documentation and conformity assessment exist. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(b) Representative keeps documentation, declaration and certificates available to authorities for the retention period. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(c) Representative handles its registration and checks the manufacturer's registration. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(d) Representative provides authorities requested conformity information in the required language. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(e) Representative forwards sample or access requests to manufacturer and ensures authority receives them. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(f) Representative cooperates with authorities on preventive or corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(g) Representative immediately passes on complaints and suspected incident reports to the manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 11(3)(h) Representative ends the mandate if the manufacturer breaches its obligations. Coming soon
Art. 11(4) The mandate cannot delegate the manufacturer's core obligations listed. Coming soon
Art. 11(5) Representative is jointly liable for defective devices if manufacturer fails obligations. Coming soon
Art. 11(6) A representative terminating its mandate must promptly notify authority and notified body with reasons. Coming soon
Art. 11(7) References to manufacturer's authority mean the authorised representative's authority. Coming soon
Art. 12 Change of authorised representativeChange of authorised representative needs a defined agreement covering listed aspects.
Art. 12(a) Agreement states mandate termination and start dates. Coming soon
Art. 12(b) Agreement states until when outgoing representative may appear in manufacturer information. Coming soon
Art. 12(c) Agreement covers document transfer, confidentiality and property rights. Coming soon
Art. 12(d) Outgoing representative must keep forwarding complaints and incident reports after mandate ends. Coming soon
Art. 13 General obligations of importers
Art. 13(1) Importers may place only compliant devices on the Union market. Coming soon
Art. 13(2) Importers must verify conformity points before marketing and act on suspected nonconformity.
Art. 13(2)(a) Importer checks CE marking and drawn-up declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(b) Importer checks a manufacturer is identified and representative designated. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(c) Importer checks labelling and instructions for use are present. Coming soon
Art. 13(2)(d) Importer checks a UDI was assigned where applicable. Coming soon
Art. 13(3) Importers must show their name and address on the device, packaging or documents. Coming soon
Art. 13(4) Importers must verify device registration and add their details. Coming soon
Art. 13(5) Importers must keep storage and transport conditions that preserve device compliance. Coming soon
Art. 13(6) Importers must keep a register of complaints, nonconforming devices, recalls and withdrawals. Coming soon
Art. 13(7) Importers must report suspected nonconformity and cooperate on corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 13(8) Importers must forward incident complaints to the manufacturer and representative immediately. Coming soon
Art. 13(9) Importers must retain copies of declarations and certificates for the required period. Coming soon
Art. 13(10) Importers must cooperate with authorities and supply samples or access on request. Coming soon
Art. 14 General obligations of distributors
Art. 14(1) Distributors must act with due care regarding applicable requirements. Coming soon
Art. 14(2) Distributors must verify listed requirements before supplying, and act on suspected nonconformity.
Art. 14(2)(a) Distributor checks CE marking and declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(b) Distributor checks the device has manufacturer-supplied information. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(c) For imports, distributor checks importer provided its identification details. Coming soon
Art. 14(2)(d) Distributor checks a UDI was assigned where applicable. Coming soon
Art. 14(3) Distributors must keep storage and transport within manufacturer conditions. Coming soon
Art. 14(4) Distributors must report nonconformity and cooperate on corrective action. Coming soon
Art. 14(5) Distributors must forward complaints and keep a register of complaints and recalls. Coming soon
Art. 14(6) Distributors must give authorities information, cooperation and free samples on request. Coming soon
Art. 15 Person responsible for regulatory compliance
Art. 15(1) Manufacturers need an in-house person with regulatory compliance expertise and qualifications.
Art. 15(1)(a) Qualification route: relevant degree plus one year's regulatory or quality experience. Coming soon
Art. 15(1)(b) Qualification route: four years' regulatory or quality experience with IVDs. Coming soon
Art. 15(2) Micro and small firms may have the compliance person on permanent call instead. Coming soon
Art. 15(3) The compliance person has minimum responsibilities listed below.
Art. 15(3)(a) Ensures devices are checked for conformity before release under the quality system. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(b) Ensures technical documentation and declaration of conformity are drawn up and current. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(c) Ensures post-market surveillance obligations are met. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(d) Ensures vigilance reporting obligations are fulfilled. Coming soon
Art. 15(3)(e) Ensures the required statement is issued for interventional performance study devices. Coming soon
Art. 15(4) Joint compliance officers must have their separate responsibilities documented in writing. Coming soon
Art. 15(5) Compliance officer must not face organisational disadvantage for properly performing their duties. Coming soon
Art. 15(6) Authorised representatives must always have a compliance person with required regulatory expertise.
Art. 15(6)(a) Expertise shown by a relevant degree plus one year regulatory or quality experience. Coming soon
Art. 15(6)(b) Expertise alternatively shown by four years of regulatory or quality experience. Coming soon
Art. 16 Cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply to importers, distributors or other persons
Art. 16(1) Distributors, importers or others take on manufacturer duties in listed circumstances.
Art. 16(1)(a) Marketing a device under one's own name makes one bear manufacturer obligations, barring agreements. Coming soon
Art. 16(1)(b) Changing the intended purpose of a marketed device triggers manufacturer obligations. Coming soon
Art. 16(1)(c) Modifying a marketed device so compliance may be affected triggers manufacturer obligations. Coming soon
Art. 16(2) Defines what changes do not count as compliance-affecting modifications.
Art. 16(2)(a) Providing or translating manufacturer information is not a compliance-affecting modification. Coming soon
Art. 16(2)(b) Outer repackaging that cannot affect the device's condition is not a modification. Coming soon
Art. 16(3) Relabelling distributors must mark their identity and keep a quality system for translations and repackaging. Coming soon
Art. 16(4) Relabellers must notify manufacturer and authority 28 days ahead and supply a notified body certificate. Coming soon
Art. 17 EU declaration of conformity
Art. 17(1) Manufacturer keeps an up-to-date, translated EU declaration of conformity with Annex IV content. Coming soon
Art. 17(2) Devices under several Union acts need one single declaration of conformity. Coming soon
Art. 17(3) Drawing up the declaration makes the manufacturer responsible for compliance. Coming soon
Art. 17(4) Commission may amend declaration content by delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 18 CE marking of conformity
Art. 18(1) Conforming devices, except performance study devices, must carry the CE marking. Coming soon
Art. 18(2) CE marking follows the general principles of Regulation 765/2008. Coming soon
Art. 18(3) CE marking must be visible, legible, indelible, and appear on packaging and instructions. Coming soon
Art. 18(4) CE marking is affixed before placing on the market. Coming soon
Art. 18(5) CE marking is followed by notified body number where applicable. Coming soon
Art. 18(6) CE marking also signals compliance with other applicable Union legislation. Coming soon
Art. 19 Devices for special purposes
Art. 19(1) Member States must not obstruct supply of performance study devices to laboratories. Coming soon
Art. 19(2) Performance study devices generally must not bear the CE marking. Coming soon
Art. 19(3) Non-compliant devices may be shown at fairs if clearly marked as demonstration only. Coming soon
Art. 20 Parts and components
Art. 20(1) Suppliers of replacement parts must ensure safety and performance and keep supporting evidence. Coming soon
Art. 20(2) Replacement parts significantly changing performance or purpose are treated as devices. Coming soon
Art. 21 Free movementMember States may not restrict compliant devices, except as the Regulation provides. Coming soon
Art. 22 Identification within the supply chain
Art. 22(1) Distributors and importers cooperate with manufacturers on device traceability. Coming soon
Art. 22(2) Economic operators must identify their supply chain partners to authorities for the retention period.
Art. 22(2)(a) Identify operators they directly supplied with a device. Coming soon

Art. 35 Assessment of the application
Art. 35(1) Authority checks application completeness within 30 days, forwards it, and drafts a preliminary assessment. Coming soon
Art. 35(2) Preliminary assessment report goes to the Commission, which passes it to MDCG. Coming soon
Art. 35(3) Commission and MDCG appoint a three-expert joint assessment team within 14 days. Coming soon
Art. 35(4) Joint team reviews documents within 90 days and an on-site assessment is planned and conducted. Coming soon
Art. 35(5) Non-compliances are discussed and listed; applicant submits a corrective and preventive action plan. Coming soon
Art. 35(6) Joint team documents remaining diverging opinions within 30 days after the on-site assessment. Coming soon
Art. 35(7) Authority evaluates the corrective plan and drafts the final assessment report. Coming soon
Art. 35(8) Authority submits final assessment report and any draft designation to Commission, MDCG and team. Coming soon
Art. 35(9) Joint team gives final opinion in 21 days; MDCG recommends within 42 days. Coming soon
Art. 35(10) Commission may adopt implementing acts detailing designation application and assessment procedures. Coming soon

Art. 38(1) Only bodies that completed assessment and meet Annex VII may be designated. Coming soon

Art. 44(1)(b) Exchange includes guidance documents for notified bodies on implementing the Regulation. Coming soon

Art. 48(13)(d) Implementing acts may specify tests notified bodies perform during sampling and documentation assessment. Coming soon

Art. 52(h) Electronic system holds certificate information. Coming soon

Art. 56 Performance evaluation and clinical evidence
Art. 56(1) Conformity must rest on scientific validity, analytical and clinical performance evidence, planned and documented by the manufacturer. Coming soon
Art. 56(2) Clinical evidence must support intended purpose and follow a continuous performance evaluation plan. Coming soon
Art. 56(3) Performance evaluation must follow a sound method and scientifically demonstrate benefit and safety.
Art. 56(3)(a) Performance evaluation must demonstrate scientific validity. Coming soon
Art. 56(3)(b) Performance evaluation must demonstrate analytical performance. Coming soon
Art. 56(3)(c) Performance evaluation must demonstrate clinical performance. Coming soon
Art. 56(4) Clinical performance studies are required unless relying on other data is justified. Coming soon
Art. 56(5) Evidence must be documented in a performance evaluation report within technical documentation. Coming soon
Art. 56(6) Performance evaluation is updated through the lifecycle; class C and D reports at least annually. Coming soon
Art. 56(7) Commission may adopt implementing acts to ensure uniform application of Annex XIII. Coming soon
Art. 57 General requirements regarding performance studies
Art. 57(1) Manufacturer ensures study devices meet general safety requirements outside the studied aspects, protecting people. Coming soon
Art. 57(2) Performance studies should resemble normal conditions of use where appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 57(3) Studies must protect subjects' rights and safety, yield reliable data, and respect data protection law. Coming soon
Art. 58 Additional requirements for certain performance studies
Art. 58(1) Certain higher-risk performance studies must meet additional Articles and Annex XIV requirements.
Art. 58(1)(a) Applies to studies with surgically invasive sampling solely for the study. Coming soon
Art. 58(1)(b) Applies to interventional clinical performance studies. Coming soon
Art. 58(1)(c) Applies to studies involving additional invasive procedures or other risks to subjects. Coming soon
Art. 58(2) Companion diagnostic studies face the same requirements, except left-over sample studies which are notified. Coming soon
Art. 58(3) Performance studies undergo scientific and ethical review including a lay person. Coming soon
Art. 58(4) Non-EU sponsors must appoint an EU legal representative. Coming soon
Art. 58(5) Studies may proceed only when all listed conditions are met.
Art. 58(5)(a) Study requires Member State authorisation. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(b) No negative ethics committee opinion may exist. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(c) Sponsor, legal representative or contact person must be established in the Union. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(d) Vulnerable populations must be appropriately protected. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(e) Anticipated benefits must justify risks, with ongoing monitoring. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(f) Subject or representative must give informed consent. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(g) Subjects must receive contact details for further information. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(h) Subjects' integrity, privacy and data protection rights must be safeguarded. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(i) Study design minimises pain and risk, with defined and monitored thresholds. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(j) Medical care is the responsibility of a suitably qualified doctor. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(k) No undue influence, including financial, on subjects to participate. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(l) Biological safety or other necessary testing has been conducted where appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(m) Clinical performance studies require prior demonstrated analytical performance. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(n) Interventional studies require demonstrated analytical performance and scientific validity. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(o) Technical safety of the device for its use must be proven. Coming soon
Art. 58(5)(p) Annex XIV requirements must be fulfilled. Coming soon
Art. 58(6) Subjects may withdraw consent at any time without detriment or justification. Coming soon
Art. 58(7) Investigators and staff must have recognised qualifications and experience. Coming soon
Art. 58(8) Study facilities should be suitable and resemble intended use facilities. Coming soon
Art. 59 Informed consent
Art. 59(1) Informed consent must be written, dated, signed, documented, with a copy and adequate time. Coming soon
Art. 59(2) Information given for consent must meet listed content and delivery requirements.
Art. 59(2)(a) Information must let subject understand study and rights.
Art. 59(2)(a)(i) Subject must understand nature, objectives, benefits, implications, risks and inconveniences. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(a)(ii) Subject must understand protection rights, including refusal and withdrawal without detriment. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(a)(iii) Subject must understand study conditions and expected participation duration. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(a)(iv) Subject must understand alternatives and follow-up if participation ends. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(b) Information must be concise, clear, relevant and understandable. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(c) Information is given in a prior interview with a qualified team member. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(d) Information must describe the applicable damage compensation system. Coming soon
Art. 59(2)(e) Information must include the study's unique identification number and results availability. Coming soon
Art. 59(3) Consent information must be prepared in writing and made available. Coming soon
Art. 59(4) Interview must attend to needs of specific populations and individuals. Coming soon
Art. 59(5) Interviewer must verify the subject understood the information. Coming soon
Art. 59(6) Subject is told a study report and lay summary will be made public. Coming soon
Art. 59(7) National law may also require a capable minor's own assent besides representative's consent. Coming soon
Art. 60 Performance studies on incapacitated subjects
Art. 60(1) Studies on incapacitated subjects need all listed conditions plus Article 58(5) ones.
Art. 60(1)(a) Legally designated representative must give informed consent for incapacitated subjects. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(b) Incapacitated subjects get study information suited to their ability to understand. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(c) Investigator must respect an incapacitated subject's explicit wish to refuse or withdraw. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(d) Only expense and lost-earnings compensation allowed; no other incentives to subjects or representatives. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(e) Study on incapacitated people must be essential, with comparable data unobtainable elsewhere. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(f) Study must relate directly to the subject's own medical condition. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(g) Scientific grounds must expect participation to yield one of two kinds of benefit.
Art. 60(1)(g)(i) Expected direct benefit to the subject outweighing risks and burdens. Coming soon
Art. 60(1)(g)(ii) Benefit to the represented population, with only minimal risk and burden to subject. Coming soon
Art. 60(2) Incapacitated subject should take part in the consent procedure as far as possible. Coming soon
Art. 60(3) Stricter national bans on studies without direct subject benefit remain unaffected. Coming soon
Art. 61 Performance studies on minors
Art. 61(1) Studies on minors need all listed conditions plus Article 58(5) ones.
Art. 61(1)(a) Legally designated representative must give informed consent for minors. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(b) Minors get information adapted to age, from staff experienced with children. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(c) Investigator must respect a capable minor's explicit wish to refuse or withdraw. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(d) No incentives beyond expense and lost-earnings compensation for minors or representatives. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(e) Study must target minor-only conditions or be essential to validate other data. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(f) Study relates to the minor's own condition or can only be done on minors. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(g) Scientific grounds must expect participation to yield one of two kinds of benefit.
Art. 61(1)(g)(i) Expected direct benefit to the minor outweighing risks and burdens. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(g)(ii) Benefit to the minor's population, with only minimal risk and burden. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(h) Minor takes part in the consent procedure in an age-appropriate way. Coming soon
Art. 61(1)(i) A minor reaching legal competence mid-study must give own express consent to continue. Coming soon
Art. 61(2) Stricter national bans on minor studies lacking direct benefit remain unaffected. Coming soon
Art. 62 Performance studies on pregnant or breastfeeding womenStudies on pregnant or breastfeeding women require all listed conditions plus Article 58(5).
Art. 62(a) Study must potentially give direct benefit outweighing risks to the woman, embryo, foetus or child. Coming soon
Art. 62(b) Without direct benefit, study allowed only if three further conditions hold.
Art. 62(b)(i) Comparable study cannot be done on women who are not pregnant or breastfeeding. Coming soon
Art. 62(b)(ii) Study must produce results that could benefit women or embryos, foetuses, children. Coming soon
Art. 62(b)(iii) Study poses only minimal risk and burden to the woman and child. Coming soon
Art. 62(c) Particular care to avoid harming the child when studying breastfeeding women. Coming soon
Art. 62(d) No incentives except compensation for expenses and lost earnings. Coming soon
Art. 63 Additional national measuresMember States may keep extra measures for military, detained, court-barred or institutionalised persons. Coming soon
Art. 64 Performance studies in emergency situations
Art. 64(1) In emergencies, consent and information may follow inclusion if listed conditions are met.
Art. 64(1)(a) Urgent, sudden serious condition prevents subject giving prior consent or information. Coming soon
Art. 64(1)(b) Scientific grounds expect a direct clinically relevant benefit or diagnosis for the subject. Coming soon
Art. 64(1)(c) Within the therapeutic window, representative's prior consent cannot be obtained either. Coming soon
Art. 64(1)(d) Investigator certifies no known earlier objection from the subject. Coming soon
Art. 64(1)(e) Study relates directly to the emergency condition and can only be run in emergencies. Coming soon
Art. 64(1)(f) Study poses minimal risk and burden compared with standard treatment. Coming soon
Art. 64(2) After emergency intervention, seek consent to continue and give information; subject consents once able.
Art. 64(2)(a) For incapacitated subjects and minors, seek representative's consent promptly and inform quickly. Coming soon
Art. 64(2)(b) For other subjects, seek consent from subject or representative, whichever is sooner. Coming soon
Art. 64(3) Non-consenting subjects or representatives must be told of the right to object to data use. Coming soon
Art. 65 Damage compensation
Art. 65(1) Member States must ensure compensation systems for study-related damage, such as insurance. Coming soon
Art. 65(2) Sponsor and investigator must use the national compensation system. Coming soon
Art. 66 Application for performance studies
Art. 66(1) Sponsor submits application electronically; Member State checks scope and completeness within ten days. Coming soon
Art. 66(2) Sponsor updates application data in the electronic system within one week of changes. Coming soon
Art. 66(3) Incomplete applications get a deadline for completion; lapse or rejection with appeal otherwise. Coming soon
Art. 66(4) Member State may extend the paragraph 1 and 3 periods by five days. Coming soon
Art. 66(5) Defines the application validation date based on notification or expiry of periods. Coming soon
Art. 66(6) Member State may request more information, suspending the assessment deadline meanwhile. Coming soon
Art. 66(7) Sets the circumstances in which the sponsor may begin the study.
Art. 66(7)(a) Low-risk specimen studies may start after validation absent a negative ethics opinion. Coming soon
Art. 66(7)(b) Other studies start after Member State authorisation, within 45 days, without negative ethics opinion. Coming soon
Art. 66(8) Commission may amend Annex XIV requirements through delegated acts. Coming soon
Art. 66(9) Commission may adopt implementing acts for uniform application of Annex XIV. Coming soon
Art. 67 Assessment by Member States
Art. 67(1) Assessors must be free of conflicts of interest and independent of sponsor and funders. Coming soon
Art. 67(2) Assessment is done jointly by enough suitably qualified and experienced people. Coming soon
Art. 67(3) Member States judge whether remaining risks are justified by expected clinical benefits.
Art. 67(3)(a) Check device meets general safety and performance requirements and subjects are protected. Coming soon
Art. 67(3)(b) Check risk-minimisation follows harmonised standards or gives equivalent protection. Coming soon
Art. 67(3)(c) Check planned installation, putting into service and maintenance of the study device are adequate. Coming soon
Art. 67(3)(d) Check reliability and robustness of study data, including statistics and design. Coming soon
Art. 67(3)(e) Check that Annex XIV requirements are met. Coming soon
Art. 67(4) Member States must refuse authorisation in listed cases and offer an appeal.
Art. 67(4)(a) Refuse if the application dossier stays incomplete. Coming soon
Art. 67(4)(b) Refuse if device or documents conflict with scientific knowledge or cannot yield evidence. Coming soon
Art. 67(4)(c) Refuse if Article 58 requirements are not met. Coming soon
Art. 67(4)(d) Refuse if any paragraph 3 assessment is negative. Coming soon
Art. 68 Conduct of a performance study
Art. 68(1) Sponsor and investigator must conduct the study per the approved plan. Coming soon
Art. 68(2) Sponsor ensures adequate monitoring, scaled to the study's characteristics.
Art. 68(2)(a) Monitoring extent considers the study's objective and methodology. Coming soon
Art. 68(2)(b) Monitoring extent considers how far intervention departs from normal clinical practice. Coming soon
Art. 68(3) Study information must be recorded verifiably while protecting confidentiality and personal data. Coming soon
Art. 68(4) Apply technical and organisational measures protecting data against unauthorised access, loss, alteration, especially over networks. Coming soon
Art. 68(5) Member States inspect study sites to check compliance with the regulation and plan. Coming soon
Art. 68(6) Sponsor sets an emergency procedure to identify and recall study devices immediately. Coming soon
Art. 69 Electronic system on performance studies
Art. 69(1) Commission sets up and maintains an electronic system for performance studies.
Art. 69(1)(a) The system generates single identification numbers for studies. Coming soon
Art. 69(1)(b) The system is the entry point for applications and notifications. Coming soon
Art. 69(1)(c) The system supports information exchange between Member States and Commission. Coming soon
Art. 69(1)(d) The system holds sponsor information including study reports and summaries. Coming soon
Art. 69(1)(e) The system handles reporting of serious adverse events and device deficiencies. Coming soon
Art. 69(2) System must be interoperable with the EU clinical trials database for companion diagnostics. Coming soon
Art. 69(3) Exchange data is restricted; other information is public unless confidentiality is justified.
Art. 69(3)(a) Confidentiality ground: protection of personal data. Coming soon
Art. 69(3)(b) Confidentiality ground: commercially confidential information, absent overriding public interest. Coming soon
Art. 69(3)(c) Confidentiality ground: effective supervision of the study by Member States. Coming soon
Art. 69(4) No subject personal data may be publicly available. Coming soon
Art. 69(5) System user interface must exist in all official EU languages. Coming soon
Art. 70 Performance studies regarding devices bearing the CE marking
Art. 70(1) Invasive or burdensome PMPF studies on CE-marked devices need notice 30 days ahead. Coming soon
Art. 70(2) Studies of CE-marked devices outside intended purpose fall under Articles 58 to 77. Coming soon
Art. 71 Substantial modifications to performance studies
Art. 71(1) Sponsor notifies Member States within a week of substantial study modifications. Coming soon
Art. 71(2) Member State assesses substantial modifications using the Article 67 procedure. Coming soon
Art. 71(3) Modifications may be implemented 38 days after notification unless refused or ethics opposes.
Art. 71(3)(a) Exception: Member State refuses on Article 67(4) or public health grounds. Coming soon
Art. 71(3)(b) Exception: ethics committee issues a negative opinion on the modification. Coming soon
Art. 71(4) Member States may extend the 38-day period by seven days for experts. Coming soon
Art. 72 Corrective measures to be taken by Member States and information exchange between Member States on performance studies
Art. 72(1) Member States may revoke, suspend, terminate or require changes if requirements are unmet.
Art. 72(1)(a) Corrective measure: revoke the study authorisation. Coming soon
Art. 72(1)(b) Corrective measure: suspend or terminate the study. Coming soon
Art. 72(1)(c) Corrective measure: require sponsor to modify any aspect of the study. Coming soon
Art. 72(2) Before acting, Member State asks sponsor or investigator for opinion within seven days. Coming soon
Art. 72(3) Member States report measures, refusals and safety terminations to others via the system. Coming soon
Art. 72(4) Withdrawn applications are made visible to Member States and Commission via the system. Coming soon
Art. 73 Information from the sponsor at the end of a performance study or in the event of a temporary halt or early termination
Art. 73(1) Sponsor reports halts or early termination within 15 days, 24 hours if safety-related. Coming soon
Art. 73(2) Study ends at last subject's last visit unless the plan says otherwise. Coming soon
Art. 73(3) Sponsor notifies each Member State of study end within 15 days. Coming soon
Art. 73(4) For multi-state studies, sponsor notifies overall end within 15 days. Coming soon
Art. 73(5) Sponsor submits study report and lay summary within a year of end. Coming soon
Art. 73(6) Commission issues guidelines on report summary content and optional raw data sharing. Coming soon
Art. 73(7) Summary and report become public, by device registration or at set times. Coming soon
Art. 74 Coordinated assessment procedure for performance studies
Art. 74(1) Multi-state studies may use a single application transmitted to all Member States. Coming soon
Art. 74(2) Member States agree a coordinating Member State within six days, else sponsor's proposal stands. Coming soon
Art. 74(3) Coordinating state directs joint assessment; certain documents' completeness is checked by each state. Coming soon
Art. 74(4) Coordinating Member State handles other documentation; final report informs all states' decisions.
Art. 74(4)(a) Coordinating state notifies sponsor of its role within six days. Coming soon
Art. 74(4)(b) Coordinating state must consider comments from concerned Member States received within seven days when validating the application. Coming soon
Art. 74(4)(c) Coordinating state has ten days to assess scope and completeness and notify the sponsor. Coming soon
Art. 74(4)(d) Sets deadlines for draft and final assessment reports and Member State comments during coordinated assessment. Coming soon
Art. 74(5) Member States may request extra information once; sponsor must reply within twelve days, pausing deadlines. Coming soon
Art. 74(6) For class C and D devices, coordinating state may extend assessment periods by fifty days for experts. Coming soon
Art. 74(7) Commission may adopt implementing acts specifying coordinated assessment procedures and timescales. Coming soon
Art. 74(8) Coordinating state's acceptable conclusion binds all concerned states, who may disagree only on limited grounds.
Art. 74(8)(a) Disagreement ground: participants would receive worse treatment than normal clinical practice in that state. Coming soon
Art. 74(8)(b) Disagreement ground: the study would infringe national law. Coming soon
Art. 74(8)(c) Disagreement ground: subject safety and data reliability concerns raised during the draft report stage. Coming soon
Art. 74(9) A not-acceptable conclusion by the coordinating state applies to all concerned Member States. Coming soon
Art. 74(10) Member States must refuse authorisation on specified grounds and provide an appeal procedure. Coming soon
Art. 74(11) Each Member State notifies sponsor of its single authorisation decision within five days of final report. Coming soon
Art. 74(12) Substantial modifications are notified electronically; assessed under coordinating state, except certain sections assessed individually. Coming soon
Art. 74(13) Commission gives administrative support to the coordinating Member State. Coming soon
Art. 74(14) Sets when all Member States must apply the coordinated procedure, with earlier voluntary application. Coming soon
Art. 75 Review of the coordinated assessment procedureCommission must report to Parliament and Council by May 2028 on experience with Article 74. Coming soon
Art. 76 Recording and reporting of adverse events that occur during performance studies
Art. 76(1) Sponsor must fully record the listed adverse events and device deficiencies in performance studies.
Art. 76(1)(a) Record adverse events the study plan identifies as critical to evaluating results. Coming soon
Art. 76(1)(b) Record every serious adverse event. Coming soon
Art. 76(1)(c) Record device deficiencies that could have caused a serious adverse event under less fortunate circumstances. Coming soon
Art. 76(1)(d) Record new findings relating to the events in points (a) to (c). Coming soon
Art. 76(2) Sponsor must promptly report listed events to Member States electronically, scaled by severity, allowing initial incomplete reports.
Art. 76(2)(a) Report serious adverse events causally related, or possibly related, to device, comparator or procedure. Coming soon
Art. 76(2)(b) Report device deficiencies that might have led to a serious adverse event. Coming soon
Art. 76(2)(c) Report new findings concerning events in points (a) and (b). Coming soon
Art. 76(3) Sponsor must also report qualifying events from third-country studies under the same plan. Coming soon
Art. 76(4) For single-application studies, report via electronic system; Member States coordinate assessment of serious events. Coming soon
Art. 76(5) For PMPF studies, vigilance provisions replace this article. Coming soon
Art. 76(6) This article still applies where a serious event is causally linked to a preceding performance study. Coming soon
Art. 77 Implementing actsCommission may adopt implementing acts detailing arrangements for this chapter.
Art. 77(a) Implementing acts may set harmonised electronic forms for performance study applications and assessments. Coming soon
Art. 77(b) Implementing acts may define how the electronic system functions. Coming soon
Art. 77(c) Implementing acts may set harmonised forms for PMPF notifications and substantial modifications. Coming soon
Art. 77(d) Implementing acts may govern information exchange between Member States. Coming soon
Art. 77(e) Implementing acts may set harmonised forms for reporting serious adverse events and deficiencies. Coming soon
Art. 77(f) Implementing acts may set reporting timelines reflecting event severity. Coming soon
Art. 77(g) Implementing acts may ensure uniform application of clinical evidence requirements for safety and performance. Coming soon
Art. 78 Post-market surveillance system of the manufacturer
Art. 78(1) Manufacturers must plan, document and maintain a risk-proportionate post-market surveillance system within their quality management system. Coming soon
Art. 78(2) Surveillance system must actively gather and analyse quality, performance and safety data over device lifetime. Coming soon
Art. 78(3) Surveillance data must be used for listed purposes and technical documentation updated.
Art. 78(3)(a) Use data to update benefit-risk determination and risk management. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(b) Use data to update design information, instructions for use and labelling. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(c) Use data to update the performance evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(d) Use data to update the summary of safety and performance. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(e) Use data to identify needs for preventive, corrective or field safety actions. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(f) Use data to find ways to improve usability, performance and safety. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(g) Where relevant, contribute data to surveillance of other devices. Coming soon
Art. 78(3)(h) Use data to detect and report trends under Article 83. Coming soon
Art. 78(4) Manufacturers must implement needed actions, inform authorities, and report serious incidents or field corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 79 Post-market surveillance planSurveillance system must rest on a plan included in technical documentation. Coming soon
Art. 80 Post-market surveillance reportClass A and B manufacturers must prepare and update a post-market surveillance report. Coming soon
Art. 81 Periodic safety update report
Art. 81(1) Class C and D manufacturers must prepare a periodic safety update report, updated at least annually.
Art. 81(1)(a) Safety update report must state benefit-risk determination conclusions. Coming soon
Art. 81(1)(b) Safety update report must set out main post-market performance follow-up findings. Coming soon
Art. 81(1)(c) Safety update report must give sales volume and user population estimates. Coming soon
Art. 81(2) Class D manufacturers submit the safety update report electronically to the notified body for review. Coming soon
Art. 81(3) For class C, make safety update reports available to notified body and, on request, authorities. Coming soon
Art. 82 Reporting of serious incidents and field safety corrective actions
Art. 82(1) Manufacturers must report serious incidents and field safety corrective actions to authorities electronically.
Art. 82(1)(a) Report serious incidents, except documented expected erroneous results covered by trend reporting. Coming soon
Art. 82(1)(b) Report field safety corrective actions, including relevant third-country ones. Coming soon
Art. 82(2) Reporting period should reflect the severity of the serious incident. Coming soon
Art. 82(3) Report serious incidents once causality is established or possible, within fifteen days of awareness. Coming soon
Art. 82(4) In a serious public health threat, report immediately and within two days. Coming soon
Art. 82(5) For death or unanticipated serious health deterioration, report within ten days of awareness. Coming soon
Art. 82(6) Manufacturers may file an incomplete initial report followed by a complete one. Coming soon
Art. 82(7) If unsure whether an incident is reportable, report anyway within required timeframe. Coming soon
Art. 82(8) Report field safety corrective actions before undertaking them, except in urgent cases. Coming soon
Art. 82(9) Periodic summary reports may replace individual reports for similar incidents if authority agrees. Coming soon
Art. 82(10) Member States must encourage professionals, users and patients to report suspected incidents and record them centrally. Coming soon
Art. 82(11) Authorities relay user-reported incidents to manufacturers, who must report or explain why not. Coming soon
Art. 83 Trend reporting
Art. 83(1) Manufacturers must report statistically significant increases in non-serious incidents or erroneous results, defining methodology in surveillance plan. Coming soon
Art. 83(2) Authorities may assess trend reports and require measures, informing Commission and notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 84 Analysis of serious incidents and field safety corrective actions
Art. 84(1) After reporting a serious incident, manufacturer must investigate promptly without altering evidence before informing authorities. Coming soon
Art. 84(2) Member States must ensure national authorities centrally evaluate serious incident and corrective action information. Coming soon
Art. 84(3) Authority evaluates incident risks and corrective action adequacy; manufacturers supply documents on request. Coming soon
Art. 84(4) Authority monitors manufacturer's investigation and may intervene or investigate independently. Coming soon
Art. 84(5) Manufacturer must submit a final investigation report electronically with conclusions and corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 84(6) For companion diagnostics, authority informs the medicines authority or EMA as appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 84(7) Evaluating authority informs other authorities of corrective actions through the electronic system. Coming soon
Art. 84(8) Manufacturer must promptly issue a field safety notice to users and enter it electronically. Coming soon
Art. 84(9) Authorities coordinate assessments in multi-state cases; manufacturer's state usually coordinates.
Art. 84(9)(a) Coordination applies to serious incidents or clusters across multiple Member States. Coming soon
Art. 84(9)(b) Coordination applies where a proposed corrective action's appropriateness is questioned across states. Coming soon
Art. 84(10) A coordinating authority does not remove other authorities' right to assess and act. Coming soon
Art. 84(11) Commission provides administrative support to the coordinating competent authority. Coming soon
Art. 85 Analysis of vigilance dataCommission and Member States monitor vigilance data for new risks and inform manufacturers. Coming soon
Art. 86 Implementing actsCommission may adopt implementing acts detailing arrangements for Articles 80 to 85 and 87.
Art. 86(a) Implementing acts may define typology of serious incidents and corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 86(b) Implementing acts may detail reporting of incidents, notices, summaries, safety update reports and trends. Coming soon
Art. 86(c) Implementing acts may set standard reporting forms, including minimum data for user-reported incidents. Coming soon
Art. 86(d) Implementing acts may set timelines for corrective action, summary and trend reports. Coming soon
Art. 86(e) Implementing acts may set harmonised forms for authority information exchange. Coming soon
Art. 86(f) Implementing acts may set procedures for designating and operating a coordinating authority. Coming soon
Art. 87 Electronic system on vigilance and post-market surveillance
Art. 87(1) Commission sets up an electronic vigilance system linked to the UDI database.
Art. 87(1)(a) System collates manufacturer reports on serious incidents and corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 87(1)(b) System collates manufacturers' periodic summary reports. Coming soon
Art. 87(1)(c) System collates manufacturer trend reports. Coming soon
Art. 87(1)(d) System collates periodic safety update reports. Coming soon
Art. 87(1)(e) System collates manufacturers' field safety notices. Coming soon
Art. 87(1)(f) System holds information exchanged between authorities and the Commission. Coming soon
Art. 87(2) System information is available to authorities, Commission and relevant notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 87(3) Commission ensures healthcare professionals and the public get suitable access to the system. Coming soon
Art. 87(4) Commission may grant third-country authorities reciprocal system access with confidentiality and data protection safeguards. Coming soon
Art. 87(5) Serious incident reports go automatically to the authority of the Member State where it happened. Coming soon
Art. 87(6) Trend reports are forwarded automatically on receipt to authorities of the Member States concerned. Coming soon
Art. 87(7) Field corrective action reports are forwarded automatically to specified Member State authorities.
Art. 87(7)(a) Recipient: the Member State where the corrective action is or will be carried out. Coming soon
Art. 87(7)(b) Recipient: the Member State where the manufacturer is registered. Coming soon
Art. 87(8) Periodic summary reports are forwarded automatically on receipt to specified authorities.
Art. 87(8)(a) Recipient: Member States taking part in the coordination procedure that agreed the summary. Coming soon
Art. 87(8)(b) Recipient: the Member State of the manufacturer's registered business location. Coming soon
Art. 87(9) Information from paragraphs 5-8 also goes automatically to the notified body that certified the device. Coming soon
Art. 88 Market surveillance activities
Art. 88(1) Authorities check device conformity and performance, using documentation review, sampling and risk-based vigilance and complaint data. Coming soon
Art. 88(2) Authorities prepare annual surveillance plans and allocate enough competent staff and resources. Coming soon
Art. 88(3) Authorities use specified powers to fulfil their checking duties.
Art. 88(3)(a) Authorities may demand documentation, information and free device samples or access from economic operators. Coming soon
Art. 88(3)(b) Authorities conduct announced and, if needed, unannounced inspections of operators, suppliers, subcontractors and professional users. Coming soon
Art. 88(4) Authorities produce an annual summary of surveillance results and share it through the electronic system. Coming soon
Art. 88(5) Authorities may seize, destroy or disable risky or falsified devices to protect public health. Coming soon
Art. 88(6) Authorities write an inspection report on compliance findings and needed corrective actions. Coming soon
Art. 88(7) Inspected operator receives the report, may comment before finalisation; final report is entered in the system. Coming soon
Art. 88(8) Member States review their surveillance every four years, sharing results and publishing a summary. Coming soon
Art. 88(9) Member State authorities coordinate and cooperate on surveillance, sharing results and possibly dividing work. Coming soon
Art. 88(10) Multiple national authorities handling surveillance and border controls must share relevant information. Coming soon
Art. 88(11) Authorities cooperate with non-EU countries' authorities on information and technical support for surveillance. Coming soon
Art. 89 Evaluation of devices suspected of presenting an unacceptable risk or other non-complianceAuthorities evaluate devices suspected of unacceptable risk or non-compliance; operators must cooperate.
Art. 89(a) Trigger: a device may endanger health or safety of patients, users or others. Coming soon
Art. 89(b) Trigger: a device otherwise fails the regulation's requirements. Coming soon
Art. 90 Procedure for dealing with devices presenting an unacceptable risk to health and safety
Art. 90(1) Authorities require operators to take proportionate corrective action, restriction, withdrawal or recall for unacceptably risky devices. Coming soon
Art. 90(2) Authorities notify the Commission, states and notified body of evaluation results and required actions. Coming soon
Art. 90(3) Operators must promptly take corrective action across the Union for all affected devices. Coming soon
Art. 90(4) If operators fail to act, authorities impose national measures and notify Commission, states and notified body. Coming soon
Art. 90(5) Notification of national measures must contain identification, origin, non-compliance reasons, risk, measures and operator arguments. Coming soon
Art. 90(6) Other Member States report extra information, measures or objections to the Commission and states. Coming soon
Art. 90(7) Absent objections within two months, measures are deemed justified and all states must apply matching measures. Coming soon
Art. 91 Procedure for evaluating national measures at Union level
Art. 91(1) Commission evaluates national measures when objected to or seemingly contrary to Union law. Coming soon
Art. 91(2) Outcome of Commission evaluation: justified measures stand, unjustified ones are withdrawn; silence after eight months means justified. Coming soon
Art. 91(3) Commission may adopt Union-wide protective measures where national measures cannot sufficiently reduce a risk. Coming soon
Art. 92 Other non-compliance
Art. 92(1) For non-risky non-compliance, authorities require the operator to end it within a set period. Coming soon
Art. 92(2) If non-compliance persists, the state restricts, recalls or withdraws the product and informs others. Coming soon
Art. 92(3) Commission may specify measures authorities take for given non-compliance types. Coming soon
Art. 93 Preventive health protection measures
Art. 93(1) After evaluation indicating potential risk, a Member State may prohibit, restrict, withdraw or recall devices. Coming soon
Art. 93(2) State taking preventive measures must immediately notify the Commission and other states with reasons. Coming soon
Art. 93(3) Commission assesses national preventive measures; no decision in six months means they are justified. Coming soon
Art. 93(4) Commission may adopt Union-wide preventive measures following its assessment. Coming soon
Art. 94 Good administrative practice
Art. 94(1) Authority measures must state their grounds; affected operators are told promptly of remedies and time limits. Coming soon
Art. 94(2) Operators get a chance to make submissions before measures, or promptly after urgent action. Coming soon
Art. 94(3) A measure is withdrawn or amended once the operator shows effective correction and compliance. Coming soon
Art. 94(4) Authorities inform the notified body and its supervising authority of measures via the electronic system. Coming soon
Art. 95 Electronic system on market surveillance
Art. 95(1) The Commission and states build and run an electronic market surveillance information system.
Art. 95(1)(a) System holds summaries of authorities' surveillance results. Coming soon
Art. 95(1)(b) System holds final inspection reports. Coming soon
Art. 95(1)(c) System holds information on devices posing unacceptable risk. Coming soon
Art. 95(1)(d) System holds information on other product non-compliance. Coming soon
Art. 95(1)(e) System holds information on preventive health protection measures. Coming soon
Art. 95(1)(f) System holds summaries of Member States' surveillance reviews and assessments. Coming soon
Art. 95(2) Information is sent immediately to concerned authorities and notified body, and open to states and Commission. Coming soon
Art. 95(3) Information exchanged between states stays non-public if disclosure could harm surveillance cooperation. Coming soon
Art. 96 Competent authoritiesMember States designate competent authorities, equip them adequately and tell the Commission, which publishes a list. Coming soon
Art. 97 Cooperation
Art. 97(1) Competent authorities cooperate with each other and the Commission; Commission organises information exchange. Coming soon
Art. 97(2) Member States join international regulatory cooperation initiatives on medical devices where appropriate. Coming soon
Art. 98 Medical Device Coordination GroupThe MDCG carries out tasks given by this regulation and the medical devices regulation. Coming soon
Art. 99 Tasks of the MDCGIntroduces the list of MDCG tasks.
Art. 99(a) MDCG helps assess applicant conformity bodies and notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 99(b) MDCG advises the Commission on the notified bodies coordination group. Coming soon
Art. 99(c) MDCG helps develop guidance for consistent implementation across designation, requirements, evaluations and vigilance. Coming soon
Art. 99(d) MDCG monitors technical progress and whether Annex I requirements remain adequate. Coming soon
Art. 99(e) MDCG contributes to developing device standards and common specifications. Coming soon
Art. 99(f) MDCG assists authorities' coordination, including a European market surveillance programme. Coming soon
Art. 99(g) MDCG gives advice on implementation issues, on its own or at Commission request. Coming soon
Art. 99(h) MDCG contributes to harmonised administrative practice across Member States. Coming soon
Art. 100 The European Union reference laboratories
Art. 100(1) Commission may designate EU reference laboratories for devices or hazards upon application. Coming soon
Art. 100(2) Introduces the tasks of EU reference laboratories.
Art. 100(2)(a) Laboratories verify claimed performance and class D compliance with common specifications. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(b) Laboratories test samples or batches of class D devices. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(c) Laboratories give scientific and technical assistance to EU bodies, states and notified bodies. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(d) Laboratories give scientific advice on state of the art for devices. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(e) Laboratories run a network of national reference laboratories and publish a list. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(f) Laboratories help develop testing and analysis methods for conformity and surveillance. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(g) Laboratories work with notified bodies on best practices for conformity assessment. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(h) Laboratories recommend reference materials and higher-order reference measurement procedures. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(i) Laboratories help develop common specifications and international standards. Coming soon
Art. 100(2)(j) Laboratories give scientific opinions to notified bodies and publish them electronically. Coming soon
Art. 100(3) On a state's request, laboratories may also be designated to verify class C devices. Coming soon
Art. 100(4) Introduces criteria that EU reference laboratories must satisfy.
Art. 100(4)(a) Laboratories need qualified, experienced staff for the relevant diagnostic devices. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(b) Laboratories need the equipment and reference material for their tasks. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(c) Laboratories need knowledge of international standards and best practices. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(d) Laboratories need suitable administrative organisation and structure. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(e) Laboratory staff must keep obtained information and data confidential. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(f) Laboratories act independently and in the public interest. Coming soon
Art. 100(4)(g) Staff must have no impairing industry interests and must declare and update interests. Coming soon
Art. 100(5) Reference laboratories form a network to harmonise testing and assessment methods.
Art. 100(5)(a) Network applies coordinated methods, procedures and processes. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(b) Network agrees on shared reference materials, test samples and seroconversion panels. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(c) Network establishes common assessment and interpretation criteria. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(d) Network uses common test protocols and standardised evaluation of results. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(e) Network uses standardised, coordinated test reports. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(f) Network develops and maintains a peer review system. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(g) Network organises regular quality assessment tests including mutual checks. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(h) Network agrees joint guidelines and standard operating procedures. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(i) Network coordinates introducing test methods for new technologies and amended specifications. Coming soon
Art. 100(5)(j) Network reassesses state of the art when requested by a state or Commission. Coming soon
Art. 100(6) Reference laboratories may receive Union funding set by Commission implementing acts. Coming soon
Art. 100(7) Laboratories may charge notified bodies or states fees for assistance or opinions. Coming soon
Art. 100(8) Commission specifies details by implementing acts under the examination procedure.
Art. 100(8)(a) Detailed rules for laboratory tasks and compliance with the criteria. Coming soon
Art. 100(8)(b) Structure and level of fees laboratories may levy for scientific opinions. Coming soon
Art. 100(9) Commission audits reference laboratories and may restrict, suspend or withdraw designation for non-compliance. Coming soon
Art. 100(10) Staff of reference laboratories fall under the confidentiality provisions of the device regulation. Coming soon
Art. 101 Device registers and databanksCommission and states encourage device registers and databanks with common principles for long-term evaluation. Coming soon
Art. 102 Confidentiality
Art. 102(1) All parties applying the regulation must keep information confidential to protect specified interests.
Art. 102(1)(a) Confidentiality protects personal data. Coming soon
Art. 102(1)(b) Confidentiality protects trade secrets and commercially confidential information. Coming soon
Art. 102(1)(c) Confidentiality protects effective implementation, including inspections, investigations and audits. Coming soon
Art. 102(2) Confidential information exchanged among authorities needs the originator's consent before disclosure. Coming soon
Art. 102(3) Confidentiality does not limit information exchange, warnings or criminal-law disclosure duties. Coming soon

Art. 103 Data protection
Art. 103(1) Member States apply the old data protection directive to processing under this regulation. Coming soon
Art. 103(2) The old EU institutions data protection regulation covers Commission processing of personal data. Coming soon

Art. 107(1) Commission is assisted by the Medical Devices Committee under the comitology rules. Coming soon

Art. 108(5) Commission notifies Parliament and Council simultaneously upon adopting a delegated act. Coming soon
Art. 108(6) Delegated acts take effect only if Parliament and Council do not object within the period. Coming soon

Art. 110(3c)(b) No significant change to design or intended purpose of legacy devices. Coming soon

Art. 110(3c)(f)(ii) Agreement deadline of 26 September 2026 for class C legacy devices. Coming soon
Art. 110(3c)(f)(iii) Agreement deadline of 26 September 2027 for class B and sterile class A devices. Coming soon
Art. 110(3d) New Regulation rules on surveillance, vigilance and registration apply to legacy devices instead of the old Directive. Coming soon

Art. 110(4) Devices lawfully marketed under the old Directive or transitional rules may remain available. Coming soon
Art. 110(5) Devices complying with this Regulation may be marketed before 26 May 2022. Coming soon
