Annex I GENERAL SAFETY AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
Annex I Chapter I GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
Annex I 1 Devices must perform as intended, be safe and effective, with risks acceptable against benefits. Coming soon
Annex I 2 Reducing risks as far as possible must not worsen the benefit-risk ratio. Coming soon
Annex I 3 Manufacturers must run a documented, continuous risk management system throughout the device lifecycle.
Annex I 3(a) Establish and document a risk management plan for each device. Coming soon
Annex I 3(b) Identify and analyse known and foreseeable hazards of each device. Coming soon
Annex I 3(c) Estimate and evaluate risks in intended use and foreseeable misuse. Coming soon
Annex I 3(d) Eliminate or control identified risks according to Section 4. Coming soon
Annex I 3(e) Evaluate production and post-market information's effect on hazards, risks and benefit-risk acceptability. Coming soon
Annex I 3(f) Amend control measures where post-market evaluation shows it is necessary. Coming soon
Annex I 4 Risk controls must follow safety principles and state of the art; residual risks communicated to users.
Annex I 4(a) First priority: eliminate or reduce risks through safe design and manufacture. Coming soon
Annex I 4(b) Where risks remain, apply protective measures such as alarms. Coming soon
Annex I 4(c) Provide safety information and user training where appropriate. Coming soon
Annex I 5 When reducing use-error risks, manufacturers must address ergonomics and user characteristics.
Annex I 5(a) Reduce risks from ergonomic features and the use environment. Coming soon
Annex I 5(b) Consider users' knowledge, training and conditions, including lay and disabled users. Coming soon
Annex I 6 Performance must not degrade dangerously over the stated lifetime under normal stress and maintenance. Coming soon
Annex I 7 Devices must withstand transport and storage without performance being adversely affected. Coming soon
Annex I 8 Known and foreseeable risks and undesirable effects must be minimised and outweighed by benefits. Coming soon
Annex I Chapter II REQUIREMENTS REGARDING PERFORMANCE, DESIGN AND MANUFACTURE
Annex I 9 Performance characteristicsHeading introducing performance characteristics requirements.
Annex I 9.1 Devices must be suitable for their purpose and achieve the manufacturer's stated performance.
Annex I 9.1(a) Analytical performance such as sensitivity, specificity, precision, accuracy and detection limits must be achieved. Coming soon
Annex I 9.1(b) Clinical performance such as diagnostic sensitivity, specificity and predictive values must be achieved. Coming soon
Annex I 9.2 Performance characteristics must be maintained throughout the stated device lifetime. Coming soon
Annex I 9.3 Calibrator and control values need metrological traceability to reference procedures or materials. Coming soon
Annex I 9.4 Performance must be specifically checked where normal use conditions may affect it.
Annex I 9.4(a) For self-testing devices, check performance obtained by laypersons. Coming soon
Annex I 9.4(b) For near-patient testing devices, check performance in relevant environments. Coming soon
Annex I 10 Chemical, physical and biological propertiesHeading for chemical, physical and biological properties requirements.
Annex I 10.1 Avoid material incompatibility with specimens that would impair analytical performance. Coming soon
Annex I 10.2 Minimise risk from contaminants and residues to patients and handlers. Coming soon
Annex I 10.3 Reduce risks from released substances and particles, especially CMR and endocrine disruptors. Coming soon
Annex I 10.4 Reduce risks from unintentional ingress of substances into the device. Coming soon

Annex I 11.1(b) Reduce microbial leakage and exposure during use. Coming soon
Annex I 11.1(c) Prevent microbial contamination of the device and specimens during use. Coming soon

Annex I 13.1 Device combinations must be safe, keep performance, and state restrictions on label or instructions. Coming soon

Annex I 13.2(b) Reduce risks from external influences like electromagnetic fields, humidity and temperature. Coming soon
Annex I 13.2(c) Reduce risks from contact with materials, liquids and gases in normal use. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C THE UDI SYSTEM
Annex VI Part C 1 DefinitionsDefines UDI terms such as AIDC, Basic UDI-DI, UDI-DI, HRI and packaging levels. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2 General requirementsHeading for general UDI requirements.
Annex VI Part C 2.1 UDI is added to, and does not replace, other labelling requirements. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.2 Manufacturer assigns and maintains unique UDIs for its devices. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.3 Only the manufacturer may put the UDI on device or packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 2.4 Use only coding standards from Commission-designated issuing entities. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3 The UDIHeading for UDI requirements.
Annex VI Part C 3.1 Assign a UDI to the device or packaging; higher packaging levels get their own. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.2 Shipping containers and logistics units are exempt from needing a UDI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.3 A UDI consists of a device identifier and a production identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.4 The UDI-DI must be unique at every packaging level. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.5 Lot, serial, software identification or expiry on the label forms part of the UDI-PI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.6 Separately sold device components get their own UDI unless part of a marked configurable device. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.7 Kits must be assigned and carry their own UDI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.8 Manufacturer assigns the UDI following the relevant coding standard. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9 A new UDI-DI is needed when changes could cause misidentification or traceability ambiguity.
Annex VI Part C 3.9(a) Change of name or trade name requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(b) Change of device version or model requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(c) Change in single-use labelling requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(d) Change in sterile packaging requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(e) Change in need for sterilisation before use requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(f) Change in quantity per package requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.9(g) Change in critical warnings or contra-indications requires a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 3.10 Repackagers or relabellers keep a record of the original manufacturer's UDI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4 UDI carrierHeading for UDI carrier requirements.
Annex VI Part C 4.1 UDI carrier goes on the label and all higher packaging levels, not shipping containers. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.2 With significant space limits, carrier may go on the next packaging level up. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.3 Individually packed single-use class A/B devices may carry the carrier only on higher packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.4 Retail point-of-sale devices need not show AIDC production identifiers on packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.5 Where other AIDC carriers appear, the UDI carrier must remain readily identifiable. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.6 Linear bar codes may split UDI-DI and UDI-PI, each distinguishable. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.7 With space limits, AIDC alone suffices, except home-use devices needing HRI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.8 Human readable interpretation follows the issuing entity's rules. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.9 If RFID is used, a standard bar code must also be on the label. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.10 Reusable devices bear a permanent UDI carrier readable after each reprocessing. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.11 UDI carrier must stay readable in normal use throughout device lifetime. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.12 Carrier on packaging is unnecessary if scannable through the packaging. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.13 For multi-part devices assembled before use, one part may carry the carrier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.14 Carrier must be placed so AIDC is accessible during normal operation or storage. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 4.15 Bar codes with UDI-DI and UDI-PI may also hold other operational data. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5 General principles of the UDI databaseHeading for general principles of the UDI database.
Annex VI Part C 5.1 UDI database must support all core data elements listed in Part B. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.2 Manufacturers handle initial submission and updates of device data in the database. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.3 Appropriate methods must validate data provided to the database. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.4 Manufacturers periodically check correctness of data for devices they have marketed. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.5 A UDI-DI's presence in the database does not imply regulatory conformity. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.6 Database must allow linking all packaging levels of a device. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.7 New UDI-DI data must be available when the device is marketed. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.8 Update the database record within 30 days of changes not needing a new UDI-DI. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.9 Database should use internationally accepted standards for data submission and updates. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.10 Database interface must be in all EU official languages, minimising free text. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 5.11 Data on devices no longer on the market stays in the database. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C 6.1 Reusable devices that are part of kits and that require cleaning, disinfection, sterilisation or refurbishing between usesHeading for reusable kit devices needing reprocessing between uses.
Annex VI Part C 6.1.1 UDI of reusable kit devices sits on the device and stays readable after reprocessing. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.1.2 Manufacturer defines UDI-PI characteristics such as lot or serial number. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2 Device softwareHeading for device software UDI rules.
Annex VI Part C 6.2.1 UDI assignment CriteriaSoftware UDI is assigned at system level; software identification serves as the production identifier. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2.2 Modifications such as new algorithms, databases, platform or interfaces require a new UDI-DI.
Annex VI Part C 6.2.2(a) A new UDI-DI is needed when a software change affects original performance. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2.2(b) A new UDI-DI is needed when a change affects software safety or intended use. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2.2(c) A new UDI-DI is needed when a change alters how data is interpreted. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2.3 Minor software revisions get a new UDI-PI, not a new UDI-DI, with manufacturer-specific identification. Coming soon

Annex VI Part C 6.2.4(d) On-screen software displays need only the human-readable UDI, not machine-readable encoding. Coming soon
Annex VI Part C 6.2.4(e) Human-readable software UDI must include the standard's application identifiers to show which issuing standard applies. Coming soon
Annex VII REQUIREMENTS TO BE MET BY NOTIFIED BODIES

Annex VII 1.1.3 Relationships with entities the notified body owns or is owned by must be defined and documented. Coming soon

Annex VII 1.1.5 Notified body must document its structure and the authority of management and influential staff. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6 Top-level management persons with overall responsibility for listed areas must be identified.
Annex VII 1.1.6(a) Management responsible for providing adequate resources for conformity assessment. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(b) Management responsible for developing operating procedures and policies. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(c) Management responsible for supervising implementation of procedures, policies and quality systems. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(d) Management responsible for supervising the notified body's finances. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(e) Management responsible for the body's activities and decisions, including contracts. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(f) Management responsible for delegating authority to staff or committees where needed. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.1.6(g) Management responsible for interaction and communications with authorities, the Commission and other notified bodies. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2 Independence and impartialityHeading for independence and impartiality of notified bodies.
Annex VII 1.2.1 Notified body must be a third party independent of manufacturers, other interested operators and competitors. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.2 Notified body must document and apply structures safeguarding impartiality, including handling conflicts of interest. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3 Introduces prohibitions on notified body management and assessment staff.
Annex VII 1.2.3(a) Staff must not be designer, maker, supplier, owner or maintainer of devices they assess. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(b) Staff must not be involved in designing, making, marketing or using devices they are designated for. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(c) Staff must not engage in activities conflicting with their independent judgement or integrity. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(d) Must not offer services undermining independence, notably consultancy to manufacturers or competitors. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.3(e) Must not be linked to consultancy organisations, though generic non-client training is allowed. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.4 Prior consultancy by new staff must be documented; three-year bar on assessing former clients. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.5 Impartiality guaranteed; pay independent of results; management interest declarations published. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.6 Public-entity-owned notified bodies must document independence from the authorities. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.7 Notified body must document that subsidiaries, subcontractors and owners do not compromise its independence. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.2.8 Notified body must apply fair, consistent terms, considering small businesses regarding fees. Coming soon

Annex VII 1.3.2 Staff must observe professional secrecy and protect proprietary rights, with documented procedures. Coming soon

Annex VII 1.6 Participation in coordination activitiesHeading for participation in coordination activities.
Annex VII 1.6.1 Notified body must follow standardisation and coordination group work and keep staff informed of legislation and guidance. Coming soon
Annex VII 1.6.2 Notified body must take guidance and best-practice documents into account. Coming soon

Annex VII 2.2(f) Quality system covers record control. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2(g) Quality system covers management reviews. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2(h) Quality system covers internal audits. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2(i) Quality system covers corrective and preventive actions. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2(j) Quality system covers complaints and appeals. Coming soon
Annex VII 2.2(k) Quality system covers continuous training. Coming soon

Annex VII 2.4 All staff must formally commit to procedures, confidentiality and independence, with written compliance statements. Coming soon

Annex VII 3.1 GeneralHeading for general resource requirements.

Annex VII 3.3.2 Maintain authorisation matrix and records of knowledge and activities for key personnel. Coming soon
